# What Paddle API keys the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every key here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, which no real
# credential is. The run serves for all three segments — once and ten characters
# over for the twenty-six of the first, once and six over for the twenty-two of
# the second, and three characters of it for the third — and with the sixteen
# character prefix in front and the two separators between, a key comes to
# sixty-nine. It is written in capitals in the two segments whose alphabet holds
# both cases, where the case is what a case is about.

patterns: paddle-api-key

# The two environments Paddle issues a key for, live and sandbox, which are one
# pattern rather than two: a key of either authenticates the same API and is
# written the same way, so a caller with reason to redact one has the same
# reason for the other. The cases below are those two shapes in the places a key
# is written.

case:     a key in an environment assignment
in:       PADDLE_API_KEY=pdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_012
out:      PADDLE_API_KEY=«paddle-api-key»

case:     a key in the bearer authorization header Paddle's endpoints are called with
in:       Authorization: Bearer pdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_012
out:      Authorization: Bearer «paddle-api-key»

case:     a sandbox key
in:       pdl_sdbx_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_012
out:      «paddle-api-key»

case:     a key in json
in:       {"apiKey":"pdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_012"}
out:      {"apiKey":"«paddle-api-key»"}

case:     a key on a command line
in:       curl -H "Authorization: Bearer pdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_012" https://api.paddle.com/transactions
out:      curl -H "Authorization: Bearer «paddle-api-key»" https://api.paddle.com/transactions

case:     the keys of both environments in one configuration
in:       PADDLE_API_KEY=pdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_012 PADDLE_SANDBOX_API_KEY=pdl_sdbx_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_012
out:      PADDLE_API_KEY=«paddle-api-key» PADDLE_SANDBOX_API_KEY=«paddle-api-key»

# The alphabets the three segments are written in, which are the classes
# Paddle's own expression spells for each of them: the lowercase letters and the
# digits for the first, and base62 — the letters of both cases and the digits —
# for the two behind it. So capitals stand in the last two segments and nowhere
# else, and a hyphen or a space ends the reading wherever it falls.

case:     capitals in the last two segments
in:       pdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789ABCDEF012345_01A
out:      «paddle-api-key»

case:     a capital in the first segment
in:       pdl_live_apikey_0123456789ABCDEF0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_012
out:      pdl_live_apikey_0123456789ABCDEF0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_012

case:     a hyphen inside the second segment
in:       pdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef-12345_012
out:      pdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef-12345_012

case:     a first segment broken by a space
in:       pdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef 123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_012
out:      pdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef 123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_012

# A first segment carrying i, l, o and u, which Crockford's base32 leaves out
# and a ULID is therefore never written with. The first segment of the key
# Paddle publishes carries none of the four, and the expression it publishes
# admits the whole of the lowercase alphabet, so the wider class is what the
# library reads and this is a key.

case:     a first segment outside crockford's alphabet
in:       pdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdefilou012345_0123456789abcdef012345_012
out:      «paddle-api-key»

# The lengths either side of each count. All three are numbers Paddle states in
# the expression it publishes, and all three are read as counts rather than
# floors: a segment one character short is no key, and a run one character
# longer than the last segment is a key and one character that belongs to no
# credential. The second of those is the price of having no boundary behind the
# match — a boundary there would drop the key rather than trim it, and a real
# key written against a character of the same class would come through whole.

case:     segments of twenty-six, twenty-two and three characters are a key
in:       pdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_012
out:      «paddle-api-key»

case:     a first segment of twenty-five characters is not
in:       pdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef012345678_0123456789abcdef012345_012
out:      pdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef012345678_0123456789abcdef012345_012

case:     a second segment of twenty-one characters is not
in:       pdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef01234_012
out:      pdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef01234_012

case:     a third segment of two characters is not
in:       pdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_01
out:      pdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_01

case:     a run longer than a key is a key and what follows it
in:       pdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_0123
out:      «paddle-api-key»3

# What a key may be written against. The prefix is the whole of the anchor and
# there is no boundary on either side of it, so a key keeps its span whatever
# word character it abuts.

case:     a key after an underscore
in:       PADDLE_API_KEY_pdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_012
out:      PADDLE_API_KEY_«paddle-api-key»

case:     a key after a letter
in:       xpdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_012
out:      x«paddle-api-key»

case:     a key before a hyphenated word
in:       pdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_012-suffix
out:      «paddle-api-key»-suffix

case:     a key at the end of a sentence
in:       the key is pdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_012.
out:      the key is «paddle-api-key».

# Two keys written together. A key can begin inside another: its opening starts
# on three lowercase characters, which a second segment may close on, and where
# the separator in front of the third segment stands behind them and the text
# carrying on from the key writes the rest of a prefix, a whole key begins
# sixty-two characters into the one in front of it. The two spans overlap and
# are redacted as one. Written with nothing at all between them the two are
# separate values, and both go.

case:     two keys with nothing between them
in:       pdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_012pdl_sdbx_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_012
out:      «paddle-api-key»«paddle-api-key»

case:     a key beginning inside the key before it
in:       pdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef012pdl_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_012
out:      «paddle-api-key»

# The prefix, which is what tells this format from text: the opening pdl_, an
# environment Paddle writes, and the marker apikey_ its own component list says
# is there to differentiate a key from anything else written with that opening.
# Each of the three below misses one of them.

case:     an uppercase prefix
in:       PDL_LIVE_APIKEY_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_012
out:      PDL_LIVE_APIKEY_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_012

case:     an environment paddle does not publish
in:       pdl_test_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_012
out:      pdl_test_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_012

case:     a run of the right lengths opening with no prefix
in:       xxx_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_012
out:      xxx_live_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef012345_012

# The other credentials Paddle issues, none of which this pattern reaches. The
# webhook secret key carries the same opening and the marker ntfset_ instead,
# and Paddle publishes one example of it and no grammar. The client-side token
# carries no pdl_ opening at all. And the keys issued before 6 May 2025, which
# Paddle calls legacy keys and states continue to work, are fifty lowercase
# letters and digits with no prefix to be found at.

case:     a webhook secret key
in:       PADDLE_WEBHOOK_SECRET_KEY=pdl_ntfset_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      PADDLE_WEBHOOK_SECRET_KEY=pdl_ntfset_0123456789abcdef0123456789_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a client-side token
in:       live_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      live_0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     a legacy key in an environment assignment
in:       PADDLE_API_KEY=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      PADDLE_API_KEY=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01

# And the text this pattern leaves alone besides.

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

case:     a log line naming the api a key authenticates against
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://api.paddle.com/transactions status=200
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://api.paddle.com/transactions status=200
